scope: Original AQA Year 1 Physics 3.2.1.4 particle interaction drawing questions; manual diagram scoring required
notes: These questions test actual sketches. The current user-facing website has on-page drawing/photo and manual criterion-based marking; do NOT claim AI verified any sketch. All diagram marks start unchecked.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Beta-minus decay: weak-boson exchange
questions.prompt: Sketch a simple particle-interaction diagram for β⁻ decay of a neutron, showing the quark that changes, the emitted weak exchange particle and both outgoing leptons. Indicate time direction. You may draw on the website or photograph your diagram. Review the four marking points manually; a typed explanation alone is not a substitute for the requested drawing. [4 marks]
markPoints: A down quark d changes into an up quark u on the quark line (neutron udd → proton uud).
A W⁻ weak boson is emitted at the d → u vertex and correctly labelled W⁻.
A separate vertex shows the W⁻ leading to an outgoing electron e⁻.
The other outgoing lepton is the electron antineutrino ν̄ₑ, shown emerging from the W⁻ vertex.
questions.modelAnswer: Time left to right: a d quark converts into u, emitting W⁻. The W⁻ connects to a second vertex with outgoing e⁻ and electron antineutrino ν̄ₑ. This describes n(udd) → p(uud) + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ; charge and electron-lepton number are conserved.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Beta-plus decay: exchanged W-plus
questions.prompt: Within a proton-rich nucleus, a proton changes into a neutron by β⁺ decay. Sketch a simple labelled particle-interaction diagram showing the quark conversion, intermediate weak boson and outgoing lepton–antilepton products. Indicate time direction and label every relevant particle. Use the drawing/manual-marking route for the four marks. [4 marks]
markPoints: An up quark u changes into a down quark d (proton uud → neutron udd).
A W⁺ weak boson is emitted at the u → d vertex and labelled W⁺.
The W⁺ connects to a vertex yielding an outgoing positron e⁺.
The remaining outgoing particle is an electron neutrino νₑ, not an electron antineutrino.
questions.modelAnswer: Time left to right: u → d + W⁺, followed by W⁺ → e⁺ + νₑ. The proton uud becomes neutron udd. Charge is conserved, and electron-lepton number remains zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Electron capture: quark-lepton interaction
questions.prompt: Inside a suitable nucleus, electron capture converts a proton and an incoming electron into a neutron and an electron neutrino. Draw a simple labelled exchange-particle diagram showing the changing quark, exchanged boson and incoming/outgoing lepton. Indicate time direction; self-review the drawn diagram using the four points. [4 marks]
markPoints: A proton up quark u changes to a down quark d as p(uud) becomes n(udd).
A W⁺ boson is emitted from u → d and connects to the electron-neutrino line.
An incoming electron e⁻ is shown at the lepton-side interaction vertex.
An outgoing electron neutrino νₑ is shown (not an antineutrino).
questions.modelAnswer: u → d + W⁺ at the quark vertex; the incoming electron absorbs W⁺ to become νₑ. Net reaction p + e⁻ → n + νₑ. A coherent time direction and correct W⁺, electron and neutrino labels are essential.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Electromagnetic scattering: virtual photon
questions.prompt: Sketch the simplest particle-exchange diagram for two electrons repelling one another by the electromagnetic interaction. Show incoming and outgoing electrons on two distinct paths, the exchange line and its particle label. Indicate time direction. Use manual mark-point review rather than automatic text scoring. [4 marks]
markPoints: Two electron lines are shown, each with an incoming e⁻ and an outgoing e⁻.
Each electron line continues through its own electromagnetic interaction vertex without changing particle identity.
An intermediate exchange line connects the two vertices, with no real photon shown as a final-state particle.
The exchange particle is labelled virtual photon γ (or virtual photon), not W⁺/W⁻.
questions.modelAnswer: Draw two separate electron paths, each entering and leaving a vertex as e⁻, with a connecting wavy virtual-photon line (γ) joining the two vertices. This represents electromagnetic exchange, not weak interaction. A mirrored or rotated but correctly labelled diagram is acceptable.
